diagnostic_evidence.quote: we actually do not need to fix how the remaining $b-1$ elements are chosen

issues.failure_explanation: For a non-first batch element $f_n$ ($\undertilde{n}<n\le\widetilde{n}$) the batch update adds all $b$ elements at once, so $f_n\in V_{\widetilde{n}}$ and $\sigma_{\widetilde{n}}(f_n)=0$, whereas $\sigma_{\widetilde{n}+1}(f_{\widetilde{n}+1})\ge\gamma\sigma_{\widetilde{n}+1}>0$; the displayed chain is false. The conclusion (P1) itself fails: for $b=2$, $\gamma=1$, $\cF=\{0,e_1,e_2,c_1,c_2\}\subset\ell_2$ with $c_i=\sqrt{1-\epsilon^2}e_0+\epsilon e_i'$, the algorithm may pick $f_0=c_1$, $f_1=c_2$ (both maximize $\sigma_0=\|\cdot\|$), giving $a_{1,1}=\operatorname{dist}(c_2,\operatorname{span}(c_1))=\epsilon\sqrt{1+(1-\epsilon^2)^2}<\gamma\sigma_2=1$. The same defect occurs in the Banach analogue (La:Psbg_B), and remark (c) after Algorithm alg:wbg is wrong: the analysis does depend on how the remaining $b-1$ elements are chosen, and even the surrogate-based choice does not yield (P1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the analysis at batch granularity: only batch-start elements satisfy the weak greedy condition, so apply the classical matrix argument (Lemma lemma:main) to the subsequence $(f_{b\ell})$ with the frozen spaces $V_{b\ell}$, yielding $\prod_{i=1}^{q}\sigma_{b(L+i)}^2 \le \gamma^{-2q}[q/m]^m[q/(q-m)]^{q-m}\sigma_{bL}^{2m}d_m^{2(q-m)}$; restrict (P1) to batch-start indices and derive all rates from this batch-granularity product inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The key lower bound on the Gram–Schmidt (and Banach functional) diagonal entries fails for all non-first batch elements, so the matrix-based error analysis of the batch greedy loses its main ingredient; the product inequalities and rate theorems built on it are unproven and in fact false as stated for large batch sizes (counterexamples in ISSUE-002/003/004).
issues.title: Lower bound (P1) on diagonal entries is false for non-first batch elements (Hilbert and Banach)
issues.why_classification: The central structural lemma is false and its proof uses an invalid inference ($\sigma_{\widetilde{n}}(f_n)=0$ since $f_n\in V_{\widetilde{n}}$); the only correct repair is a different proof architecture (batch-start subsequence), and that repair changes the main rate guarantees (constants acquire $b^{-\alpha}$ factors). No local fix preserves (P1) together with the advertised rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses the false (P1) via $\prod_i|a_{n+i,n+i}|\ge\gamma^K\prod_i\sigma_{N+b-1+i}$, which fails for non-first batch elements. The inequality is independently false: in $\ell_2$ let $\cF=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{j\ge1}\{c_{j,1},c_{j,2}\}$ with $c_{j,k}=e^{-j^2}e_j+\epsilon e'_{j,k}$, $b=2$, $\gamma=1$. In batch $\ell$ the two points of cluster $\ell+1$ are the unique top two by the frozen surrogate $\sigma_{2\ell}$, so the algorithm is forced to pick both; hence $\sigma_{2\ell}=e^{-(\ell+1)^2}$ and $d_m\approx e^{-(m+1)^2}$. With $N=0$, $K=20$, $m=13$: LHS $=\prod_{i=1}^{20}\sigma_{1+i}^2=e^{-4\sum_{\ell=1}^{10}(\ell+1)^2}=e^{-2020}$ but RHS $=[20/13]^{13}[20/7]^7\sigma_1^{26}d_{13}^{14}\approx e^{5.60+7.35-26-2744}\approx e^{-2757}$, so LHS $>$ RHS, a contradiction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false inequality by the batch-granularity product inequality $\prod_{i=1}^q\sigma_{bL+i}^2 \le \gamma^{-2q}[q/m]^m[q/(q-m)]^{q-m}\sigma_{bL}^{2m}d_m^{2(q-m)}$, proved by applying Lemma lemma:main to the batch-start subsequence $(f_{b\ell})$; this is strictly weaker and yields rate constants with a factor $b^{-\alpha}$.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central technical inequality is false for $b\ge2$ whenever the Kolmogorov $n$-width decays exponentially with $\alpha(b-1)>1$ (e.g. $b=2$, $\alpha=2$); the rate theorems in Theorem col:wbg_hilbert and Corollary Cor:expDecay, which are proved from it, are unproven and in fact false for large $b$, and the numerical upper bound $\widetilde\sigma(n)=Ce^{-c(2/3)^\alpha n^\alpha}$ fitted from the false Corollary is theoretically unjustified.
issues.title: Product inequality in Theorem th:wbg_hilbert is false for $b\ge2$ (exponential width regime)
issues.why_classification: The main technical inequality of the paper is false in a regime the paper explicitly targets (exponential $n$-widths); every repair replaces it by a strictly weaker batch-granularity inequality and materially worsens the derived rates for large $b$, so the advertised guarantee is abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: only need to be modified in a minor manner to obtain corresponding results for the batch greedy case

issues.failure_explanation: (i) is false for large $b$: in the cluster example with $b=16$, $\alpha=1$ ($c_{j,k}=e^{-j}e_j+\epsilon e'_{j,k}$, sixteen points per cluster) each batch is forced to pick one cluster, so $\sigma_{16\ell+15}=e^{-(\ell+1)}$ while $\min_{m<16\ell}d_m^{(16\ell-m)/(16\ell)}\approx e^{-4\ell}$, and $e^{-(\ell+1)}>\sqrt2\,e^{-4\ell}$. (iii) and Corollary Cor:expDecay are false for large $b$: on this example the actual exponential rate constant of the batch algorithm is $c_0b^{-\alpha}$ (e.g. $c_0/16$ for $b=16$, $\alpha=1$), but (iii) claims the $b$-independent $c_02^{-(\alpha+1)}3^{-\alpha}$ and the Corollary claims a loss of only $(2/3)^\alpha$; for $b>3\cdot2^{1+1/\alpha}$ with $c_0<\ln C_1$ the claimed constant is below the actual one, so the bound fails. (The exponent in the printed statement of (i) is $\frac{n-m}{m}$ while its proof derives $\frac{n-m}{n}$.) Part (ii) is unproven: its proof relies on the false product inequality, and the correct batch-granularity analysis yields only $\sigma_{bq}\lesssim(q/\ln q)^{-\alpha}$ for polynomial widths, a logarithmic loss that (ii) does not contain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (i), (iii) and the Corollary from the batch-granularity product inequality $\prod_{i=1}^q\sigma_{bL+i}^2\le\gamma^{-2q}[q/m]^m[q/(q-m)]^{q-m}\sigma_{bL}^{2m}d_m^{2(q-m)}$, giving $\sigma_{bq}\le\sqrt2\gamma^{-1}\min_{m<q}d_m^{(q-m)/q}$ and the exponential rate constant $c_0b^{-\alpha}\frac{\alpha^\alpha}{(\alpha+1)^{\alpha+1}}$ instead of the $b$-independent $c_02^{-(\alpha+1)}3^{-\alpha}$; replace the Corollary's $(2/3)^\alpha$ loss by the true $b^{-\alpha}$-type loss; re-prove or weaken (ii) (the correct argument available gives a logarithmic loss).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised rates — $\sigma_{n+b-1}\le\sqrt2\gamma^{-1}\min_m d_m^{(n-m)/n}$ in (i), the stretched-exponential rate with $b$-independent constant in (iii), and the Corollary's claim that batching costs only a factor $(2/3)^\alpha$ in the rate constant — are false for large $b$ (e.g. $b\ge5$ for $\alpha=1$ in (i); $b\ge3$ for $\alpha=2$ in (i); $b\ge9$ for $\alpha=2$ in (iii); $b\ge13$ for the Corollary at $\alpha=1$, the regime used in the numerics): the true rate constant can be as bad as $c_0b^{-\alpha}$. The introduction's claim that the classical proofs 'only need to be modified in a minor manner' is thereby misleading, and the numerical upper bound fitted from Corollary Cor:expDecay is unjustified.
issues.title: Rate bounds in Theorem col:wbg_hilbert (i), (iii) and Corollary Cor:expDecay are false for large batch sizes
issues.why_classification: The headline theoretical guarantees (rate preservation with only a $(2/3)^\alpha$ constant loss) are false for large batch sizes — the true loss is $b^{-\alpha}$ — and repairing them needs a new proof architecture with $b$-dependent constants, a major loss of the paper's main result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof relies on the same false (P1) from Lemma La:Psbg_B. The inequality is independently false by the same cluster example, which lives in the Banach space $\ell_2$: with $b=2$, $\alpha=2$, $N=0$, $K=20$, $m=13$, LHS $=e^{-2020}$ while RHS $=2^{20}20^7(\sum_{i=1}^{20}\sigma_i^2)^{13}d_{13}^{14}\approx2^{20}20^7(2e^{-2})^{13}e^{-2744}\approx e^{-2726}$, so LHS $>$ RHS. Consequently theo:Banach (i) and (iii) are false for large $b$ (e.g. $b=16$, $\alpha=1$: $\sigma_{16\ell+15}=e^{-(\ell+1)}$ exceeds the claimed bound $\approx(16\ell)^{1/4}e^{-4\ell}$), and the polynomial rate (ii) is unproven (the correct batch-granularity analysis gives a weaker bound).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the batch-granularity product inequality in Banach spaces via the batch-start subsequence $(f_{b\ell})$ with the functionals $\lambda_j$, and restate theo:Banach with $b$-dependent rate constants (exponential rate constant $\sim c_0b^{-\alpha}$).
issues.overall_effect: The Banach-space counterparts inherit the same false ingredient: the product inequality th:wbg_banach is false, and theo:Banach (i) and (iii) are false for large batch sizes; the appendix's claim to generalize the classical Banach results is not valid as stated.
issues.title: Banach-space product inequality (th:wbg_banach) and rate theorem (theo:Banach) are false for large batch sizes
issues.why_classification: Same root and same counterexample as the Hilbert case: the Banach product inequality and the advertised Banach rates are false for large $b$ and require the batch-granularity re-proof with $b$-dependent constants; the appendix's guarantees are abandoned as stated.
